transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in — what brings you here today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

What finally got me in here is just... well, I've been a little scattered lately, I guess. Nothing too serious, I promise, I'm a very safe driver and a hard worker. But over these last few months, my mind just sort of keeps jumping around. I'll catch every little CB radio chirp, or get distracted by a fuel price sign, or just get totally swept up in a new idea. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but because of it, I've been missing some details I normally never miss. Just small things, really—like misplacing a client’s delivery note, or forgetting who I promised to call back. I feel bad about it, and I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to get it checked out. Does that make sense to come see you for something like that?

Thinking back, did you notice similar problems with distractibility or restlessness when you were a child or teenager, or is this the first time in your life you've experienced this kind of difficulty?

No, no, nothing like this when I was younger. I was always a pretty focused kid, you know? I did fine in school, kept my head down, did my chores... I was never one of those kids bouncing off the walls or getting into trouble for not paying attention. 

I mean, sure, maybe I'd daydream a little during a boring class, but who doesn't do that, right? Nothing that ever caused any real problems. This whole... scattered feeling, the mind jumping around... it's really just been the last few months. That's why I thought I should come in, because it's so out of character for me. I just want to get back to being my usual, reliable self. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Over these past few months, have you also noticed feeling unusually energetic, upbeat, or needing much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Well, I guess... I mean, I have been sleeping a bit less, but honestly, it hasn't felt like a bad thing. I hope it doesn't sound crazy, but I've actually felt pretty good. 

Most nights lately, I'll sleep maybe three, sometimes four hours tops. But the funny thing is, I wake up way before daylight and I just feel... ready to roll, you know? Not worn out or dragging at all. I actually feel like I have plenty of energy to get the day started. I figured it was just my body adjusting to the schedule or something. Is that... is that something I should be worried about? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by mentioning it.
Have you ever had a period in the past, lasting two weeks or more, where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, no, not really. I mean... everybody has a bad day on the road now and then, right? But no, never two straight weeks of feeling down or anything like that. 

I've always been the kind of guy who just pushes through and tries to keep a positive attitude. I don't really let things get to me too much, you know? I've got a job to do, so I just focus on that and keep moving forward. I hope that's okay to say? I'm trying to give you the best answer I can, I just... I haven't really ever dealt with that sort of deep sadness. Is that the kind of information you need?

Have these past few months of high energy and racing thoughts caused any serious problems—like conflicts with coworkers or family, financial or legal trouble, or situations where people around you have expressed serious concern about your behavior?

Well... no, definitely no legal trouble or anything extreme like that. I always try to keep things professional and do the right thing. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture here—there have been a few minor hiccups. 

Like on the job, I've had to ask dispatch, and even a couple of clients, to repeat details that I really should have been tracking. And I think a couple of my sales follow-ups might have slipped through the cracks recently, mostly just because I was... well, chasing too many ideas at once. It's really not like me to drop the ball, I swear. 

And at home... this is a little hard to admit, but... I can tell my wife and daughter have been kind of walking on eggshells around me lately. I'm supposed to be the one helping out and keeping things steady for them, and I know I'm just adding strain right now instead. I feel pretty terrible about it, to be honest. I hope I'm not coming across like a bad guy or a bad provider, I'm just trying to be upfront with you so we can get this sorted out. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have these symptoms ever gotten so intense that you were unable to complete your work shifts or had to stop working altogether, even for a short time?

No, no, I've never missed a shift or had to stop working. I take a lot of pride in my work, you know? I've been driving and doing sales for a long time, and being reliable is just... well, it's really important to me. 

Even when my thoughts are moving a mile a minute or I'm feeling a little scattered, I always make sure I show up and get the job done. I mean, my family counts on me, and my boss counts on me. I'd never let this get in the way of providing for them. I push through whatever's going on and just focus on the road. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to reassure you that I'm still functioning fine at work, I haven't let things fall apart or anything like that. Is that helpful to know?

During these past few months, have you noticed feeling unusually confident or special—like you have great abilities or plans—or have you made any impulsive decisions, like spending a lot of money or taking risks you normally wouldn't?

Well, I definitely haven't done anything crazy with money or taken any dangerous risks, I promise you that. I'm a family man, so I always try to be sensible with our finances and safety. 

But... I guess I have been feeling pretty, I don't know, fired up lately? Maybe a little too confident in some areas. Like, I recently got it in my head that I could completely rebuild our whole driver training program myself. I just felt this... this huge surge of certainty that I could make it run so much better than the bosses ever could. 

Which sounds a little arrogant when I say it out loud, I know. Especially since management and training really isn't my lane at all. I'm just out there driving and doing sales. I just wanted to help the company out and I felt really capable of fixing everything, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm full of myself or causing trouble. I just had a lot of ideas and felt really good about them. Is that the kind of confidence you were asking about?

Would people who don't know you well—like new clients or strangers you interact with briefly—also notice that something seems different or off about you lately, or is it really only your close family and coworkers who've picked up on these changes?

Oh, no, definitely not strangers. I mean... I really try to put my best foot forward with people I don't know, especially new clients on my route. I always make sure to keep it very professional. I would honestly be mortified if someone I just met thought I was acting... well, weird, or off in any way. 

So, no, I don't think anyone who just interacts with me for a few minutes would have any clue at all. It's really just my wife and daughter, and maybe the guys I work with every single day, who see the... the extra energy and all that. I always make sure I'm polite and respectful to the public, no matter how fast my brain is going. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, does that show I'm still keeping things under control where it counts? I really try my best not to let this affect how I treat people.
Has this behavior caused any serious arguments, conflicts, or a real breakdown in your relationship with your wife or daughter, or is it more that they've just noticed you seem different?

Well, I wouldn't say there's been any... serious breakdowns or huge fights, no. I really try to keep the peace at home. I love my wife and daughter very much, and I want them to be happy. 

But... I guess I have noticed that things are a little tense lately. My wife and daughter, they kind of seem like they're walking on eggshells around me sometimes. Which really bothers me, because I'm supposed to be helping and supporting them, not adding strain, you know? I hate the idea that I'm making them uncomfortable. 

And, um... I know I said work was fine, and I haven't missed any shifts, which is true! But... I guess I have had a few minor slip-ups lately. Just little things. Like, I've had to ask dispatch or a couple of clients to repeat details that I normally would have remembered. And maybe one or two sales follow-ups slipped through the cracks because I was just... chasing too many ideas at once with that training program thing. 

I'm really trying to get a handle on it, though. I don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job or being a bad husband. I'm still trying my best. Is it normal to have a few little hiccups like that when you're feeling this energetic?
